uncited: This method manages memory peaks during the structure updates (density control) and image supply phases of 3D Gaussian Splatting training.
It solves the problem of high GPU memory usage caused by concurrent old and new state layouts during densification and high-resolution image decoding.
The method consists of two primary subsystems: Structure Update Management and Image Supply Management.
- **Inputs**: List of Gaussian parameters (position, scale, rotation, SH coefficients, opacity), optimizer states, statistics, and a set of training images (compressed).
- **Outputs**: Updated Gaussian parameters, optimizer states, and statistics ready for the next training step, with bounded peak memory usage.
**Gaussian State**: Contains parameters, optimizer state, and statistics.
Layout is rebuilt only once per density control cycle.
**Prefetch Queue**: A fixed-capacity queue holding decoded images.
**Pinned Memory Buffer**: Used for transferring leaf regions.
Standard methods rebuild the Gaussian layout after every clone, split, parent removal, or pruning action, creating intermediate layouts with concurrent old and new state.
-   **Host Memory Pressure**: The CPU-assisted path increases host RSS.
Stores predecoded images on the host CPU to reduce GPU structure-update peaks during training.
It uses CPU assistance for structure updates instead of repeated GPU rebuilding.
This lowers the structure-update peak from 12.83 to 8.68 GiB (32.4% reduction), but raises RSS from 6.30 to 13.37 GiB and adds 11.7% training time on five 5K scenes.
-   Controls high-resolution working sets effectively.
-   Reduces GPU memory peaks during structure updates.
-   Adds training time due to CPU-GPU transfers and decoding overhead.
-   When GPU memory is the bottleneck during structure updates.
-   When training on high-resolution images (5K and above).
-   When training time is critical and GPU memory is sufficient.
The method addresses the memory peaks observed in full training of 3D Gaussian Splatting, particularly during density control and image supply phases.
